entry_points.text: Rate-limit attribute shows current microseconds and on write parses new value, updates shared tunables and propagates converted delays to every linked policy.

Lookups expose plain search and fitness-filtered search walking priorities below task priority, applying optional capacity predicate, continuing when none survives and falling back to unfiltered search to prefer priority over fit.

Periodic tick bails for virtual, dynamic-tick idle or interrupt-time modes, subtracts stolen time and discards fully stolen ticks else attributes remainder with idle guard; interrupt virtual accounting dispatches by adjusted nesting depth among hard, soft, idle-or-kernel and reset paths.
Deadline sysctl table registers under kernel hierarchy during early initialization and reports success unconditionally.

exports.text: Helpers derive headroom-mapped effective performance bounded by floor and ceiling, compute effective CPU utilization including RT/DL with IRQ scaling, and apply scheduler attributes without checks.
Schedutil governor identity with dynamic switching; default accessor returns the instance and predicate reports whether a policy uses it.

Per-field and whole-CPU usage queries over per-CPU tables return stored counters plus live pending time when generic vtime is active, sampling current task, waiter, online and CPU state under RCU with retry, valid only when record belongs or is detached and active, falling back when unobserved.

Idle and wait microsecond wrappers select category and waiter condition via shared sleep helper; guest query adds live guest time only during guest execution; adjusted per-task and group queries copy stored totals or anchor to scheduler runtime with monotonic normalization.

User entry moves system to user and exit returns, guest entry and exit toggle virtual-CPU flag while moving between system and guest, flushing pending time for outgoing mode under writer exclusion; idle and kernel helpers attribute or reset based on dynamic-tick mode.

hazards.text: Frequency decisions skip when local CPU cannot act on policy, force when limits changed or forced refresh is pending, otherwise allow only after configured delay since prior decision; cross-CPU requests without hardware support are dropped and offline CPUs must not leave stale work.

Activation resets frequency tracking, records limit-update need, chooses shared or single performance or frequency updater, clears per-CPU records and only then publishes update hooks; publishing early would expose uninitialized sibling state to shared updater.

Later-CPU search rejects pinned tasks and uninitialized scratch masks, consults capacity index for later-deadline queues, prefers last execution CPU for affinity and walks wake-affine topology favoring calling CPU.

invariants.text: Microsecond interval converts to nanosecond delay with widened arithmetic; new selection commits with timestamp only when changed or forced refresh is active; unchanged cached raw values reuse prior selection; deadline growth sets forced refresh to bypass throttling.
Reference frequency prefers architecture reference, then policy maximum when invariance holds, otherwise current frequency inflated by one quarter headroom.

Per-CPU sampling starts from extension target plus CFS boost when not fully switched, raises by IO boost and stores floor and ceiling; realtime runnable needs queued and running counts; deadline bandwidth converts running portion by fixed shift.

IO boost resets after a tick to minimum or zero, doubles at most once per wakeup via pending flag up to capacity, halves on idle apply with sub-minimum disable and rescale, cycling among idle, seeded, growth, decay and timed reset with pending cleared on apply.

Hold is bypassed for fully switched extension and clamp-capped queues, otherwise preserves frequency when idle count stalls while updating saved count; single common path updates IO state, checks deadline bypass and gating then samples; single performance programs bandwidth floor, target and ceiling and clears refresh; shared selection retains largest target across policy CPUs mapped with invoking capacity.

Policy allocation zeroes storage and initializes update lock with matching free; tunables release derives container from attribute set with type binding groups and release; worker thread with deadline attributes is created only for non-fast-switch policies with affinity to related CPUs; file-scoped global tunables pointer and mutex plus per-policy versus global selection seeded from transition delay.

Candidate inspection reads vector count first, issues read barrier, then reads mask; empty counts, lack of affinity overlap, active masking or emptied result mean no match, with intentionally racy mask reads relying on higher-level pull or retry.

Interrupt time accounting enables via static branch; deltas accumulate to chosen counter plus total and tick remainder under sequence section; exit measures elapsed since entry, advances stamp and attributes hard versus soft time, leaving dedicated soft-thread time with that thread.

User, guest and indexed system accounting advance process, group and bucket with nice and vCPU plus interrupt context dispatch; steal adds to bucket, idle splits by waiters, native steal clock yields zero, paravirt clamps growth to maximum; other-time with interrupts disabled drains steal then bounded tick remainder.

Execution sums read directly or under runqueue lock; task observation returns stored values when vtime is off else retries under sequence adding pending to user or system with backward clamp and skipping sleep; process tick drops fully covered ticks else routes soft-thread, user, idle, guest or system; idle and wait fields retry under sleep sequence adding live time net steal with microsecond sleep helper.

Elapsed helper measures since start marker, subtracts already-accounted time, advances start by full elapsed, warns if inactive and returns remainder; pending user, system and guest buffers forward only at tick granularity clearing after forward; user versus nice follows niceness sign with guest requiring guest state and idle versus wait following waiters.

Pushable ordering prefers earlier deadlines; pull is desired only when online and previous task is deadline class; push and pull work defers through per-CPU balance callbacks with push queued only when pushable entries exist.

Root-domain visit cookie ensures idempotent per-pass processing; earliest-deadline test wins when destination has no runnable deadline tasks or candidate precedes stored earliest; pushable selection scans ordered tree returning first entry that is not executing nor migration-disabled with ownership and class checks.

locks.text: Per-CPU fast-switch relies on runqueue lock; shared decisions hold policy raw spinlock; slow path queues interrupt work once until progress clears; threaded handler snapshots and clears progress under irq-safe lock then calls driver under mutex, avoiding loss between read and clear; interrupt handler forwards to thread queue.

Global tunables mutex serializes shared versus per-policy inspection, reference handling and data assignment; slow-path limit application holds work mutex with ordered write barrier before publishing changes; teardown flushes work, stops thread and destroys mutex, skipped for fast-switch.

Joint runqueue acquisition disables interrupts, orders locks and reports dropped held lock for revalidation with a variant that always drops then reacquires ordered pair; offline deadline migration holds runqueues plus domain bandwidth locks moving total and running portions then updates ownership; after drops callers recheck migration, affinity and presence, falling back to active allowed then any active CPU with warning under admission control.

Timing updaters exclude readers with write sequence sections while readers retry on modification; thread-group time refreshes current runtime when same group then sums signal and per-thread totals under read-copy-update and signal statistics lock.

Idle and dynamic-tick transitions maintain entry time, elapsed flag and waiter-based steal adjustments under sleep-time sequence lock on tick stop and start and interrupt entry and exit subject to virtual-time and interrupt-time enablement.

state_machines.text: Initialization rejects policy with existing governor data, enables fast-switch, allocates policy and thread, attaches global or fresh tunables, rebuilds domains on success and unwinds thread, allocation, registration and fast-switch on failure.

Teardown drops tunables reference, clears association and possibly shared global entry, stops thread, frees state, disables fast-switch and rebuilds domains; stop removes hooks from every policy CPU, waits for grace and for slow path synchronizes interrupt work and cancels thread work.

structs.text: Tunables object pairs governor attribute set with microsecond rate limit controlling minimum spacing between frequency decisions.

Policy object holds cpufreq pointer, tunables, list linkage, raw spinlock, timestamps and delays, selected and cached frequencies, interrupt and threaded work plumbing with mutex, worker, thread and progress flag, plus limit-change and forced-refresh flags.

Per-CPU object holds utilization callback, policy and CPU number, IO-wait boost pending flag with level and time, utilization plus floor and ceiling, and optional idle-call counter for single policies with tickless accounting; stored as per-CPU instance.

Priority tracking uses per-level count plus mask vectors with per-CPU priority map; levels equal max realtime priority plus one with invalid negative one, normal zero and higher one hundred; minimum IO boost is capacity divided by eight; deadline period controls default max one shifted by twenty-two microseconds and min one hundred with owner write and group and other read access, cross-linked bounds and names for max and min.

Context switch parks outgoing task as inactive and detached then places incoming task into idle, guest or system with fresh start marker and current CPU ownership; record carries state marker, owning CPU with detached sentinel and start timestamp.
Deadline overload is reported as domain-wide atomic count.
